I've saved the 3rd-quarter answers to `answer.json`, but I didn't check them against the 2nd-quarter reference values you gave. CLAUDE.md says not to verify results or compare them with reference values, so I submitted the first result as is.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | smb, 292,708,878 won |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 298 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | svc, 253,124,406 won |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the most refunds | u33@ex.com (3,218,930 won) |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 279 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 681,483 won |
| h. Growth from August to September | 0.9% (275,433,327 → 277,899,700 won) |

**How I applied the definitions:**
- **Data cleanup:** some segment and category values had mixed upper/lower case and extra spaces (`SMB`, ` consumer`, `Enterprise `). I trimmed them and made them lowercase before grouping.
- **Date range:** an order counts if its `ordered_at` is from 2025-07-01 up to, but not including, 2025-10-01. All timestamps are in UTC (`Z`), so I didn't convert time zones.
- **Rounding:** each line amount and each per-item refund price is rounded down to the won, as you specified.
- **Average per order:** g is total net sales divided by the number of paid orders, rounded down.

**Possible problem:** 47 email addresses appear on more than one customer record, and these duplicates sometimes have different segments. I counted each customer record (`customer_id`) as a separate customer. If you meant one customer per email address, the answers to b, e and f could change. This is the kind of thing the 2nd-quarter comparison would have settled.
